content: I’ll trace `SessionDocument`’s branch semantics, then compare both in-memory and SQLite timeline projections against realistic lane-move/fork flows. I’ll remain read-only and base the verdict on concrete APIs, callers, and tests.

content:
CONFIRMED

- `SessionDocument.entries()` returns every entry in the mutation log, while `branch("main")` follows the current main-lane leaf through `parentId`: `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\core\ji-session-api\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\session\tree\SessionDocument.java:1001-1042`.
- `SessionDocument.snapshot()` incorrectly builds its transcript from `entries()`, not `branch("main")`: same file, lines 65-78.
- `MemoryHostStore.timeline()` consumes that snapshot transcript: `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\applications\ji-host-core\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\MemoryHostStore.java:72-81`.
- SQLite similarly projects all message entries: `E:\Projects\Code\AI\Ji\ji-java\adapters\ji-host-sqlite\src\main\java\io\github\diodeme\ji\host\sqlite\SqliteHostStorePersistence.java:437-462`.
- Public APIs make the divergence constructible: append `m1`, append `m2`, `moveLane("main", Optional.of("m1"))`, append `m3`. Then `branch("main")` is `[m1,m3]`, but `entries()`, snapshot, Memory timeline, and SQLite timeline contain `[m1,m2,m3]`. An alternate lane likewise leaks its lane-only messages.
- SQLite has an additional navigation defect: its stable-prefix algorithm only truncates by size or appends by index; equal-sized or prefix-divergent branch changes leave stale projected rows.
- `fork()` itself copies only `branch(laneName)`, so a newly forked document is correct; the confirmed defect applies to moved/branched source documents and projections derived from all entries. No production `moveLane` caller currently exists, but the operation is exposed through `SessionDocument` and revision-CAS `SessionRepository.update`.
